_comment: The hazard model's numbers (core/hazardModel.ts). EVERY value here is a gameRule: tuned so Panaji plays as a fair build-and-protect game. None is a measurement or claims to come from a study. Water is in 'game metres', compared with the DEM ground height of each tile; the real Panaji ground is real, the water is game design.

surge._comment: Cyclone storm surge. Level at the landfall site = baseM + perStrengthM x strength. Each hex the water moves it loses: seaM along the open sea, channelM up a river or creek (it funnels further there), beachM over sand, landM over land.

flood._comment: Monsoon river flood. Sources are the upstream part of the river (riverIndex up to sourceShare of the mouth index). Level at a source = baseM + perStrengthM x strength. It loses channelM per hex down the river and creeks, wetlandM per hex into the wetland (khazan) fields, landM per hex up the banks.

compound._comment: Cyclone and flood together. The surge holds the river back at the mouth: every channel tile also gets a backwater level = backwaterShare x (surge level at the mouth) x (riverIndex/mouthIndex)^backwaterExponent on top of the flood's own level there.

defence._comment: A defence protects the area round it: water within radiusHex hexes stands lower by metresPerResilience x its resilience (scaled by maturity and wear) x falloff[distance]. On a tile only the strongest defence of each kind counts; different kinds add up (layered defence), to at most stackCap times the strongest single one there, so a mix of defences does more than many of one kind. pathShare of that also slows water passing through its own tile and its neighbours. Negative resilience (sand mining, a resort) lets water through more easily. Engineered structures fail when the water on their tile is deeper than failureThreshold x failDepthPerUnit, and then give no protection; nature defences over overwhelmSeverity x overwhelmDepthPerUnit protect at their overwhelmed share and are worn. However many defences stand round a tile, together they hold back at most maxProtectionM there: the front line of a big storm is lost even behind the best defences, and what a player saves is the streets behind it.

landfall._comment: Where a cyclone can come ashore: open-sea tiles on the shore, ordered along the coast. The schedule picks a forecast centre and the real site is within jitterSites of it (bounded: a player who defends the forecast cone is never caught out). The forecast cone shown to the player narrows from coneFarSites half-width when the storm is first in view to jitterSites by the time the forecast locks.
